title: Phase 3: cascade of triplet stages, training variants one factor at a time
question: For a small cascade (2 stages, M = 4, K_th = 16, FIR7; 1 136 RM), what do shared C, stage-wise training, ridge initialization and dropping the symmetries change?
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: the winning factor is used in any further cascade runs (E040 confirm results, E041)
value_filter.answered_in_literature: partly: PB-DBP reports +0.04-0.1 dB for independent vs shared C on their data; not on ours
value_filter.needed_for_main_claim: no; it tunes the cascade family

decision_if_positive: use the factor that wins by > 2 std in later cascade experiments
decision_if_negative: keep the E040 setting (independent, joint, zero init, symmetric)

variants.v3_stagewise_freeze: stage 1 trained alone (100k), then stage 2 alone with stage 1 frozen (100k), fresh Adam
variants.v4_ridge_init_stage0: stage 1 starts from the closed-form ridge solution (stage init; symmetric projection = orbit average), stage 2 at zero
variants.v5_free_no_symmetry: merged weights as free complex numbers (no C_{-m,-n} = C_mn = -C*_{-m,n})

rule_draft.status: DRAFT: to be confirmed by the user before the first run; must not change after results are seen
rule_draft.factor: a variant differs from v1 if |test mean difference| > 2 std over 5 seeds (std = the larger of the two); sign as measured
